summary: The root وهن (whn) signifies weakness, languor, or enervation. It describes being rendered faint, lax, or cowardly, losing energy or resolve. The verb أَوْهَنَهُ means to weaken or unnerve someone.
lane: 4 أَوْهَنَهُ ذ He, or it, weakened him: [ rendered him languid, languid and faint, or lax in the joints; enervated him, unnerved him, or broke his energy; rendered him cowardly: (see وَهَنَ :)] (S, Msb, K:) and , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) but the former is the better, (Msb,) and . (S, K.)

headwords.def: He was, or became, weak, or infirm, in an affair, and in operation, and in body; (Msb:) and so said of a bone: (Bd, and Jel in xix. 3:) and he was, or became, languid, languid and faint, or lax in the joints; (TA, Bd in iii. 140;) enervated, unnerved, or broken in energy; (Bd, ubi suprà;) cowardly. (TA, Jel in iii. 140.) See also 4.

The period about midnight; (S, K;) or the time after an hour, or a short period, ( سَاعَة,) of the night: (JK, K, TA:) or when the night is departing. (S.) See إِنْىٌ.
عِرْقُ الوَاهِنَةِ The cephalic vein: see فَلِيقٌ.
I. q. وَنَاةٌ, q. v.; and see أَنَاةٌ.
Weak, languid, unable to rise: see عُدَوَآءُ.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
